diagnosis.policy_state: Root Cargo.toml:310-326 defines workspace lints (rust unsafe_code=forbid; clippy all/pedantic warn, unwrap_used/expect_used/todo/dbg_macro/print_stdout/print_stderr warn, four targeted allows). crates/kernel/eliot-platform-windows/Cargo.toml does NOT inherit ([lints] workspace = true absent); it declares its own tables. Uncommitted working-tree diff (git diff HEAD) shows the crate table previously carried ONLY all/pedantic/module_name_repetitions/must_use_candidate (+rust unsafe_code=allow, unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn=deny) and the change ADDS dbg_macro/expect_used/missing_errors_doc/missing_panics_doc/print_stderr/print_stdout/todo/unwrap_used - i.e. the eight-entry restoration mirroring workspace values exactly.
diagnosis.expansion_mechanism: Because the crate opt-outs of workspace lints, at HEAD unwrap_used/expect_used were simply NOT ENABLED for this crate, so clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings passed despite 250 unwrap/expect call sites. Restoring the lints re-enabled them; -D warnings promotes every warn to an error, so all 250 sites became hard failures at once, plus pedantic too_many_lines on over-long production functions (owned_directory_retirement.rs:329 spans lines 328-452, ~124 lines > default 100). The expansion is arithmetic, not a regression: the debt predates restoration; restoration made it visible.
diagnosis.test_vs_production_split: All 250 unwrap/expect occurrences sit inside #[cfg(test)] code; production unwrap()/expect() count is ZERO. Per-file verification matched every hit line number against cfg-test module boundaries (lib.rs cfg-test at 13343/15080/15090, hits 15191-15941; package_staging.rs cfg-test 4259/4423, hits 4451-5677; owned_directory_retirement.rs cfg(all(test,windows)) at 651, hits 657-731; tcp_listener_owner.rs cfg-test 373, hits 381-575; installer_root.rs tests from 2055, hits 2707/2722/2817; installer_authority_key.rs and supervision_authority_key.rs zero hits). Production .unwrap_or(0) at owned_directory_retirement.rs:293,403 is not flagged by unwrap_used.
diagnosis.manifest_residual_risk: The fix duplicates workspace values instead of inheriting them, so drift remains possible; today the clippy tables are value-identical. The one real divergence is deliberate: rust unsafe_code=allow vs workspace forbid is required because this FFI crate calls SetFileInformationByHandle etc. under unsafe (owned_directory_retirement.rs:611-621 with SAFETY comment); full inheritance is impossible without a workspace-side carve-out. This needs an explicit Architecture-owner note rather than silent divergence.

remediation_lanes.content: Split fn retire_owned_directory_exact_inner (328-452) into private phase helpers: bind_and_verify_directory (validation+handle identity, 340-369), retain_and_verify_children (371-422), commit_delete_dispositions (424-451); keep the public signature and orchestration body under 100 lines so no allow is needed. Preserve before_delete hook semantics and CommittedUnknown ordering exactly.
remediation_lanes.discriminator: existing tests exact_tree_is_retired_by_handle_identity and concurrent_child_substitution_is_blocked_and_extra_create_fails_precommit (which call the inner fn directly) must pass unchanged before and after

remediation_lanes.content: largest lane; place one module-scoped attribute pair at the top of each test mod; convert shared fixture/helper returns to Result<T, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> with ? so most expects collapse into propagation; keep bare expects only where they are the assertion oracle

remediation_lanes.note: fixture() is the ideal Result conversion target; identity() helper becomes ?-propagating

remediation_lanes.smallest_lane: candidate for full honest-Result conversion with zero allows

result.lane_rules: one writer per file (R6/I17.15); lanes are disjoint by file so they parallelize safely; order P1 before T4 (same file); each lane proves itself via cargo check -p eliot-platform-windows --all-targets plus its own ModuleTestCapsule slice, never workspace-wide cargo

production_refactor.required: exactly one production finding family in scope: too_many_lines at owned_directory_retirement.rs:329 (328-452)
production_refactor.approach: mechanical phase extraction into private #[cfg(windows)] helpers within the same file; no signature changes; no error-type changes; no new unwraps introduced
production_refactor.explicitly_not_required: no production unwrap/expect exists to convert (verified zero); mark_delete SAFETY block stays untouched

prohibited_shortcuts: crate-wide or file-top-level #![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)] outside #[cfg(test)] modules - masks future production panics
removing or downgrading unwrap_used/expect_used/pedantic in either Cargo.toml (policy lowering, violates W0-02 premise)
reverting the manifest to omit the restored lints to make warnings disappear
switching -D warnings off for the crate or excluding it from --workspace gates
deleting or #[ignore]-ing the affected tests to shrink findings
catch_unwind wrappers or debug_assert replacements for expects
hand-waving the unsafe_code=allow divergence instead of recording it as an owner-signed platform exception

scoped_allow_assessment.verdict: contractually acceptable when and only when strictly test-scoped
scoped_allow_assessment.basis: the 250 findings are exclusively #[cfg(test)]; expect() in tests doubles as the assertion oracle, so blanket Result-conversion trades oracle clarity for ceremony; module-scoped attributes inside #[cfg(test)] mod blocks cannot leak into production compilation units, are grep-auditable, and match the precedent already accepted in-tree (five existing function-scoped clippy allows); under A0.6 this qualifies as a bounded deviation provided each attribute carries owner/review condition implicitly through the W0-02 lane record
scoped_allow_assessment.preferred_order: 1) Result<T, Box<dyn Error>> + ? conversion for fixture/helper functions, 2) module-scoped #[allow(clippy::expect_used)] (add clippy::unwrap_used only where a test genuinely uses it) placed at mod level, never file level, 3) leave assertion-oracle expects in place under the scoped allow
scoped_allow_assessment.non_negotiable: any occurrence later found in production code must be converted to typed Result, never allowed

result.proof_ceiling: Static-analysis ceiling: no cargo/clippy execution was permitted, so the authoritative finding list and exact error count are derived arithmetically (250 cfg(test)-confined sites + observed >100-line production function + unknown additional pedantic findings across the 15k-line lib.rs and package_staging.rs that only the compiler can enumerate); cfg-boundary classification was done by line-number comparison against cfg(test)/cfg(all(test,windows)) anchors and could misclassify if an item-scoped cfg(test) attribute governs a region between anchors (checked for the five mid-file anchors in installer_root.rs; none contain unwrap/expect); non-Windows cfg paths and the test-support feature combination were not compiled; the claim that clippy tables are value-identical to workspace was verified by direct list comparison, not by cargo resolution.

accepted_findings: Restoring the effective lint policy exposes large test-target debt.
No lint suppression or policy weakening is accepted.
integration_disposition.proof_ceiling: read-only source audit; root Cargo diagnostics remain acceptance evidence
